title: Giving free days to all challenge winners at once sends one request per winner, one after another
what: When the owner taps the button to give (or skip) the prize for every winner of a finished challenge, the panel asks the server for each winner in turn and waits for each answer before the next. On slow 4G that is about a second per winner, so 50 winners keeps the owner waiting close to a minute, and one failed request stops the rest without saying which winners were done.
expected: All winners are handled in one request, or in parallel, and the screen says clearly who got the days and who did not.
who: owners of busy gyms running challenges
fix_line: Send all winners in one server call and report each winner's result

title: The Visits screen goes through the gym's whole check-in history about eight times after every check-in
what: Each check-in at the desk changes the visit list, and the Visits screen then works out again, from every visit the gym ever had, the Losing the habit count, who is in today, the day's register, the 30-day chart, the summary and the busy hours. A gym with 500 members and a few years of check-ins has tens of thousands of visits, so each tap gets slower on a cheap desk phone as the gym ages.
expected: Only the recent days the screen shows are re-counted, and the Losing the habit count is worked out once, not on every check-in.
who: desk staff at big, older gyms
fix_line: Count from the last few weeks of visits only and keep the risk count from refreshing on each tap

title: The day's register, a batch list and the Losing the habit list draw every row at once
what: The search box shows at most 8 matches, but the register of a day, a picked batch and the Losing the habit list have no limit and no Show more. In a 500-member gym a busy day or a long risk list puts hundreds of cards with buttons on the page at once, which scrolls and redraws slowly on a cheap phone.
expected: Long lists show the first part and a Show more, like the member search and the measurement history already do.
who: desk staff and owners of big gyms
fix_line: Show the first 50 rows with a Show more button

title: Each member who leaves makes the database read the leaderboard records of every gym
what: When a member leaves, the clean-up removes their leaderboard days and board line and blanks the phone on their challenge wins. None of the three lists has an index that starts with the member, so each leave reads all of those lists for every gym. The days list grows with every gym and member, so this gets slower as MettleUp grows. The database's own advisor flags two of the three.
expected: Each of the three lists has an index on the member, so a leave touches only that member's rows.
who: every gym, as the platform grows
fix_line: Add an index on the member for the three leaderboard lists
